speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Finance if he will clarify the $5.3 billion of "Capital Reserve" in PUB's accounts and whether this represents surplus funds that are at the disposal of the Government or PUB.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: There has been some confusion about what the "Capital Reserve" in the Public Utilities Board's (PUB's) accounts represent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Mr Pritam Singh referred to it in his speech during the Debate on the President's Address, and I note that the Workers' Party subsequently posted a video clip on its Facebook page questioning why the water price increases were necessary when the PUB's Capital Reserve has increased from $3 billion to $5.3 billion over the last decade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: But this is completely inaccurate and demonstrates a basic misunderstanding of accounting fundamentals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Rather, most of the funds are already invested in PUB's Property, Plant and Equipment – in accounting terms, it is PPE – and that includes the upgrading of waterworks, water reclamation plant expansions and investment in water treatment processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: It is either ignorant or disingenuous to link the water price increase with the PUB's Capital Reserve, as there is absolutely no basis to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: I hope this clarification will set the record straight.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: I also hope the Workers’ Party will refrain from distorting the facts to mislead the public.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: In fact, having posted the video on its Facebook page and demanded that the Government clarify the matter, I hope the Workers' Party will now also post this explanation on Facebook to correct the record.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And this is something we will look at.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I just want to follow up with a question to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the rising demand for water in the coming years, what are the upcoming major investments in the water supply infrastructure in the next decade?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What amount of capital expenditure is the Government envisaging?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And how are we going to fund them?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Is this going to be from PUB’s balance sheet, or from the Government’s injections?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, I mentioned this figure during the COS debate as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are investments for the development of the new Tuas Reclamation Plant, the renewal of Chestnut Avenue and Choa Chu Kang Waterworks and other pipeline projects.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The investments will be financed through a combination of either accumulated surpluses – where there are – and borrowings, because these accumulated surpluses from previous years, as I have mentioned, are not sufficient to finance all of our infrastructure needs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, PUB will have to borrow in order to finance these future investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the investment quantum that we are talking about from FY2017 to FY2021.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Going beyond that, there are also other major projects that are in the pipeline, including, for example, Phase 2 of the Deep Tunnel Sewerage System, as well as the redevelopment of Kranji Water Reclamation Plant and the expansion of Changi Water Reclamation Plant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are in the pipeline, and the specific quantum and details will be announced at an appropriate juncture.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The bottom line is that we still need to make investments in our water infrastructure and these are very important investments to ensure that we have a secure and resilient water supply, both today and into the future.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The PUB Annual Report 2017 does not refer to notes on Capital Reserve, like its Annual Report in 2016.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On capital reserve, just a short paragraph, "Section 40 of the Public Utilities Act 2002 requires the Board to finance a reasonable proportion of its capital expenditure from internal sources.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The capital reserve has been utilised to account for the yearly transfer of the retained earnings to finance the Board’s property, plant and equipment", just like the Minister mentioned.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And then it goes on to say, "The capital reserve comprises the accumulated transfers from retained earnings and amounts paid by Government bodies and private developers towards the capital outlay for the provision of utility, facilities completed before 1998." Can the Minister please share some information on the last aspect of this note, how much is this amount that has been transferred prior to 1998; what are we talking about here?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as the footnote explains, these are accumulated surpluses over the years that PUB has been able to earn.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But none of these surpluses are left in cash.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the essence of what I am trying to say.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We think of reserves as cash, but Capital Reserve happens to be an accounting term.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It means that the funds were used to invest in PPE, and there are some technicalities about the specific assets, the date of the assets, but those are technical points because the main thrust of what I am trying to say is that there is no surplus cash lying around in PUB's books for PUB's disposal.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: All of it is being invested in water infrastructure already and we will need more of that for our future water supply as well.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: So, all these investments will be solely borne by Singaporean consumers through water price hikes, or should the Government also provide grants, some capital grants, for instance, for the investment, thereby lightening the consumers' burden?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, when you look at the water system today, there is a component which is charged out to consumers, PUB recovers the costs, the revenues, and then uses that to finance part of the water system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But there is also a significant part of the water system which is already financed by the Government through the taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, these details are in PUB's accounts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You can see very clearly what is the amount that is charged out to consumers and are taken in as revenue on PUB's books, and the amount that is taken as grants from the Government.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We may need a new video series on how to be an accountant.
